texts: good. the Council, the half-shifts, Coraline Ash as the one they are approved for, the Harbor Station and day 80 of Year 1 are all carried.
good. the "so" link between the retirement and the station standing unstaffed is recorded, with the retirement ordered first, and "senior Keeper" is kept as a senior kind of keeper.

bad: "for the first time" is silently dropped — nothing in the parse records that this was her first lighting, so it reads as an ordinary lighting like any other. Stating it as its own clause keeps the content: "Coraline Ash lit the lantern of the Harbor Station at sundown, and she had never lit it before."
good. "stood beside" is recorded as a past position of Pell relative to Coraline Ash rather than as an event, which is the right reading for a postural clause.
good. the catching and the manner "cleanly" are both carried, and no unstated link between the wick and the lantern is invented.
good. the burning and the mire-essence are carried, with mire-essence filed as a kind of essence.
good. the producing is carried and mist-light is filed as a kind of light.
good. the same mist-light is reused and "at night" is carried.
good. the mist-light links back to the previous sentences, and the nightmoths become a set the parse can refer to again.
good. "after sundown" is recorded as a lower bound on when the landing happened, which is the right shape for an open-ended "after".

mixed: everything in the sentence is carried, but the parse files the threads as something the leaving created or altered rather than as something deposited unchanged, so a later question about what the moth left behind looks in the wrong slot. Making the depositing explicit fixes it: "The nightmoth deposited silken threads on the lantern."
good. Coraline Ash, the lantern and "that night" are all carried; no calendar day is attached, because the passage never dates the lighting that night points back to.
good. the two times are read as two separate joinings, one at midnight and one at the third watch, each with the Harbor Station as the place.
